change: Amended Immigration Act allows employers' associations to take in foreign trainees.
Employment Service Act enacted, formalizing the admission of migrant workers first allowed in 1989.
Technical Intern Training introduced, together with the Japan International Training Cooperation Organization (month approximate).
Minimum Allowable Wage cut by 5%, from HK$3,860 to HK$3,670, citing the recession.
Act to Implement the ICCPR and ICESCR adopted; in force December 2009.
EU issues an IUU 'yellow card' to South Korea (lifted April 2015).
Supreme Court recognizes the Migrants' Trade Union.
EU issues an IUU 'yellow card' to Taiwan (lifted June 2019).
Employment Permit System starts under the Act on the Employment of Foreign Workers (2003); the industrial trainee system it replaced is abolished in 2007.
Act for Distant Water Fisheries adopted; crew regulations follow in January 2017.
Rule requiring migrant workers to leave Taiwan for one day before a new contract deleted (Employment Service Act Art. 52(4)).
Technical Intern Training Act in force; Organization for Technical Intern Training created.
Specified Skilled Worker status introduced, with change of employer allowed within a field.
US Department of Labor adds Taiwan-caught fish to its forced-labor goods list.
Ratifies ILO C29, C87 and C98 (in force April 2022).
Government-to-government arrangement with Indonesia for fishers on coastal vessels.
Long-term Retention of Migrant Workers Program: after six years' service, workers may move to intermediate skilled status (from 30 April).
Fisheries and Human Rights Action Plan, first phase 2022–2025.
Minimum wage for distant-water foreign crew raised from US$450 to US$550; minimum medical insurance.
Ratifies ILO C105 (in force July 2023).
Plan for distant-water crew: voyages capped at 12 months; companies to drop agencies that deduct wages.
Talks on an Indonesia–Taiwan MOU for distant-water fishers end without agreement.
Diet passes the act replacing Technical Intern Training with Employment for Skill Development (Act No. 60 of 2024, promulgated 21 June).
WCPFC adopts a measure on crew labor standards, to apply from 2028.
Laos begins sending fishing crew on the E-10-2 visa.
Minimum Allowable Wage raised to HK$5,100.
Crew regulations amended: wage reporting and a wage-reserve mechanism.
Second-phase action plan 2026–2029; US$570 minimum for newly recruited distant-water crew.
Indicators for identifying trafficking victims issued by the Ministry of Gender Equality and Family (Notice 2026-32), applied to migrant fishers.
Ministry of Justice confirms a route for E-9 and E-10 workers to the skilled-worker status (E-7-4).
Minimum Allowable Wage raised to HK$5,220 for contracts signed from 3 October.
Employment for Skill Development scheduled to start.
EU Forced Labour Regulation applies, including to catch from Taiwan's fleet and goods from the other three.
